create.name: Vairocana Zen Monastery
create.bio:
Vairocana Zen Monastery is a Chinese Chan (Zen) temple in Garden Grove, in Orange County, California, founded and led by its abbot, Venerable Master Miao Tsan. Its stated purpose is to make clear the heart of Zen's teaching on Mind, and it has a dedicated Zen hall for meditation alongside landscaped Zen gardens. Branches have since opened in Arcadia, California, and in Mexico City. Master Miao Tsan writes in traditional Chinese; his books include Just Use This Mind and The Origin Is Pure, and his commentary on the Gateless Gate koans was launched in Taipei in 2026. He has taught meditation at universities, hospitals and on broadcast media across the United States, Mexico, Taiwan and mainland China.

The monastery's core training is meditation classes and intensive Zen retreats lasting three or seven days, and those unable to attend in person can join classes online. It also keeps the Buddhist calendar with ceremonies such as the Buddha's birthday bathing rite and a yearly commemoration of Huineng, the Sixth Patriarch. Its YouTube channel, 禪問 Zen Answer, opened in 2025 and carries the abbot's Mandarin teachings, including a long verse-by-verse series on the Platform Sutra, plus short bilingual answers to practical questions about the mind and practice.

Channel is the abbot's own (handle @shihmiaotsan, title 禪問 Zen Answer); Master Miao Tsan is not on Spiritpedia. Listed here as the monastery because the channel names the monastery as its contact; owner may prefer a teacher listing.
Teaching is in Mandarin (long Platform Sutra series); many uploads are short English cartoon clips with high views (possibly promoted). Only talks and bilingual Q&A chosen.
Site's books are in Chinese with NT$ prices through Taiwanese retailers: not added as books (no ISBN/ASIN read).
